questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Chad?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Chad article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Chad?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Chad article.

questions.proof: Arabic and French are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is slightly smaller than _____ and slightly larger than South Africa.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “smaller”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Chad article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: It is slightly smaller than Peru and slightly larger than South Africa.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country's capital is 1,060 kilometres (660 mi) from the nearest seaport Douala, _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Douala”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Chad article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: The country's capital is 1,060 kilometres (660 mi) from the nearest seaport Douala, Cameroon.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the north is _____, to the south is the Central African Republic, to the east is Sudan, and to the west are Cameroon, Nigeria, and Niger.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “north”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Chad article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: To the north is Libya, to the south is the Central African Republic, to the east is Sudan, and to the west are Cameroon, Nigeria, and Niger.
